title: Embo-Harness: Towards Understanding Frontier-Model-as-Policy Harness
excerpt: Frontier multimodal models exhibit extraordinary generalization in generating robot actions from observations and instructions, enabling a new paradigm in which they serve directly as policies within closed-loop robotic harnesses. However, the design principles of such harnesses, and the capabilities underlying their strong performance, remain unclear. We present Embo-Harness, a framework for systematically studying frontier-model-as-policy harnesses. We investigate four components of the robotic agentic loop, namely, prompting, planning, action execution, and tool use, and distill six empirical findings into a practical recipe. This recipe prioritizes interfaces that exploit the model's…

ai.summary: Embo-Harness presents a framework to study how frontier multimodal models can be used directly as closed‑loop robotic policies, analyzing four key components of such harnesses.
ai.why: Helps researchers design and evaluate model‑as‑policy systems for robotics applications.

title: World Models as Native Latent Action Models
excerpt: Large and diverse video sources, such as egocentric human video and heterogeneous robot recordings, carry rich dynamics but come either without actions or without a shared action space. Latent action models (LAMs) can recover these dynamics, but they train their inverse- and forward-dynamics models (IDM, FDM) from scratch, trading off pixel reconstruction against latent capacity and accuracy. Pretrained video world models natively generate high-fidelity dynamics, yet represent them densely, entangled across all layers. ai.summary: The paper proposes using pretrained video world models as native latent action models to recover dynamics from video sources without a shared action space, avoiding the trade-offs of training inverse and forward dynamics models from scratch.
ai.why: Provides a more efficient path for building world models that can generalize across diverse robot and human video data for control tasks.

title: Self-WSP: Can Language Models Improve Themselves Through Weight-Space Programming?
excerpt: Frontier language models can now read and edit the weights of a neural network much like code and thereby improve a small model, an approach known as Weight-Space Programming (WSP). We further explore applying WSP to a language model itself, which we call Self-WSP. Specifically, Qwen3.5-0.8B reads its own weights, proposes an edit, and then continues with the edited weights as both problem solver and editor. We find many cases of genuine self-improvement. Self-edits can raise GSM8K accuracy from 11.8% to 62.2% and MATH500 accuracy from 7.0% to 32.2%, sometimes by changing only 16 parameters, and in some cases repeated self-editing keeps improving the model. ai.summary: Qwen3.5‑0.8B reads its own weights, proposes edits, and continues inference, achieving self‑improvement that raises GSM8K accuracy after the weight edits.
ai.why: Demonstrates that language models can autonomously refine themselves via weight‑space programming, opening new avenues for model maintenance.

title: 3AGameFactory-Motion: Agentic Rigging and Reliable Complex Motion Generation for Diverse 3D Assets
excerpt: Animating arbitrary 3D assets from instructions requires both structural inference and motion control, yet existing motion benchmarks mostly cover conventional human or animal skeletons with simple instructions. We introduce DivDynBench, which evaluates rigging and motion generation across six morphology categories, with instructions requiring multi-phase part coordination and explicit timing, angle, repetition, and trajectory constraints. With large language models, we systematically compare three common paradigms: specialized motion generation, video generation followed by motion recovery, and direct agent-driven generation. We analyze their control capabilities, cross-morphology…

ai.summary: The paper introduces DivDynBench, a benchmark for evaluating agentic rigging and motion generation across six diverse 3D asset morphologies, and uses LLMs to compare methods for handling complex, multi-phase motion instructions.
ai.why: Offers a rigorous testbed for developers working on 3D animation pipelines and generative motion control for non-standard assets.

title: Plan4D: Generative Plannable 4D Worlds
excerpt: Most world models for future prediction prioritize aestetic quality of generated videos, but offer only weak physical grounding and limited geometric consistency over time, due to the lack of explicit 4D modeling. In this paper, we introduce plan4d, a possible next milestone towards building a generative plannable 4D world model that predicts future RGB videos together with dense 4D geometry, including depth, cameras, point clouds, and scene flow from an observed scene context and text-specified actions. Since training data with paired actions and dense 4D annotations is inherently scarce, plan4d leverages the complementary priors of foundational video generators and 3D reconstructors…

title: WeightCode: Installing New Capabilities into Neural Networks via Weight-Space Programming
excerpt: Neural networks encode learned capabilities in their weights, yet extending those capabilities with explicit task knowledge remains a fundamental challenge. Here we show that Weight-Space Programming (WSP), in which executable programs read, construct or modify a network's weights directly, can install new capabilities within trained neural networks. WeightCode, a WSP framework, uses a frozen language model to write executable weight programs that install new computations into trained neural networks using task knowledge and their existing weights, without gradient-based training. Once installed, the new capabilities run independently of the language model. Given a grammar or eight…

ai.summary: WeightCode is a framework where a frozen language model writes executable programs that directly modify a neural network’s weights to install new capabilities without retraining.
ai.why: Provides a practical way to extend existing models with additional functions via weight‑space programming.

title: AutoPILOT: A Visual Agent Harness for Real-Time Gameplay
excerpt: Multimodal foundation models can play video games well when the game waits for them, but often fail when it keeps running. We find that much of this gap lies in the harness, which decides what the model sees, what it remembers, and how its outputs become actions over time. Existing harnesses such as VISTA improve the first two, yet turn each model call into at most one action, so the agent acts only as often as its model thinks. We introduce AutoPILOT, which changes the third: in each model call, the model can send a primitive action, start an open-loop macro, or write a closed-loop controller that keeps playing from the screen without further model calls until it hands control back. title: ViDecide: Teaching Video Diffusion Models to Reason and Plan Step by Step
excerpt: Current leading video generation models can synthesize highly realistic videos, while still frequently violating physical and logical constraints in multi-step reasoning and planning, even after training with large-scale reasoning data or existing diffusion RL methods. We attribute these failures to the conventional video training paradigm, which treats a solution as a fixed-length clip rather than a chain of decisions. We present ViDecide, a decision-centric framework that trains video diffusion models to predict state transitions causally and decide when to stop, with a decision-focused training schedule. ai.summary: ViDecide is a decision-centric framework that trains video diffusion models to reason and plan step-by-step, addressing failures in physical and logical constraints found in conventional clip-based training.
ai.why: Improves the logical consistency and physical plausibility of generated videos, which is critical for applications requiring reliable simulation or planning.

title: Innata-0: A Native Embodied World System with Model-Agent Co-Design
excerpt: The physical world is open-ended, dynamic, and partially observable. While foundation models have advanced embodied intelligence, standalone models struggle with long-horizon execution, and simply integrating models with agents may lead to inconsistencies between planning and physical control. To support reliable and adaptive behaviors in the physical world, we introduce Innata-0, a native embodied world system. Innata-0 jointly designs an embodied world-action model and an agent to combine their complementary strengths. title: Let the Fixer Decide: Training a Code Localizer from the Fixer's Likelihood
excerpt: Code localizers are usually trained to predict the files a reference patch edits, but the code a fixer needs to read is not the same as the code it changes. We propose Fixer-Guided Localization (FGL): the localizer proposes several localizations, a frozen fixer scores each by how likely it makes a verified patch, and the localizer is trained on these scores with weighted supervised fine-tuning, without running tests and without reinforcement learning. We build the full pipeline on Gemma 4 E4B for the Kaggle Gemma-4 Developer Agent competition, from 1,629 test-verified Kimi K3 trajectories. ai.summary: Fixer-Guided Localization (FGL) is a training method where a code localizer is supervised by a frozen fixer model's likelihood scores for verified patches, improving code localization without reinforcement learning or test execution.
ai.why: Offers a more efficient and stable training paradigm for coding agents that need to identify relevant code files before applying fixes.

title: Unlocking the Power of Loops in Pretrained LLMs with Loop Residuals
excerpt: Looped Transformers iterate a shared block of layers to increase computation without adding parameters, offering stronger performance and test-time scaling. However, this power has so far required training from scratch and yielded only modest gains for LLMs. Finetuning existing models into loops is far cheaper, yet also brings only marginal gains over SFT. We propose LoopRes, an effective, scalable, and simple approach that turns loops into significant and consistent gains for pretrained LLMs. Building on Attention Residuals, LoopRes lets each looped layer attend directly to the outputs of earlier loops. ai.why: Offers a cost-effective technique to improve model performance and test-time scaling for existing models.

title: A Glimpse of Training VLMs as Foundation Models for Robotic Manipulation
excerpt: Recently, GPT-6 Astra demonstrates strong generalization in robot control, yet limited disclosure of its training leaves open how such capabilities can be reproduced. We introduce nanoAstra, an approach to training vision-language models (VLMs) for generalizable manipulation that combines semantic action modeling with capability-preserving supervised fine-tuning (CP-SFT). nanoAstra represents robot behavior as semantic steps composed of reusable, parameterized action primitives, guided by explicit progress descriptions. title: ViDiHand2: Unifying Video Diffusion Priors and Hand Geometry for 3D Hand Motion Reconstruction in the Wild
excerpt: Learning robot manipulation from egocentric human videos requires accurate metric 3D hand motion. Recent methods leverage pretrained video diffusion model (VDM) priors to recover occluded hands directly from full-frame videos, but their appearance-based depth regression generalizes poorly to unseen cameras. In this work, we propose ViDiHand2, a geometry-driven framework that reformulates VDM-based hand depth estimation from direct regression into fine-grained geometric constraint solving. title: Distilling Visual Agents from Limited Interaction Experience
excerpt: How much interaction experience is needed to distill a capable visual agent? We study learning from few tasks and recorded interaction histories. Our framework selects representative trajectories using skill-context coverage and ordered visual-decision similarity. On-policy distillation (OPD) learns through fresh interaction on selected tasks or fresh student responses at fixed histories. Across Navigation, Sokoban, and spatial mapping, even one online training task supports transfer to other tasks. ai.summary: A framework for distilling visual agents from limited interaction data uses skill‑context coverage and visual‑decision similarity to select trajectories, enabling transfer across tasks with as little as one online training task.
ai.why: Developers can build visual agents with fewer interactions, reducing data collection costs.

title: Motion Mamba 2.0: Autoregressive Diffusion Mamba for Long-Horizon Humanoid Control
excerpt: Long-horizon, real-time controllable motion generation is essential for interactive animation and humanoid robotics, where an agent must respond to changing instructions and spatial goals while moving. Existing autoregressive diffusion methods generate motion incrementally, but bounded attention caches limit access to distant history, while repeated denoising introduces substantial inference overhead. We present Motion Mamba 2.0, a Mamba-based root-body diffusion architecture that integrates local attention, resumable recurrent states, and persistent content memory (PCM) for long-horizon controllable motion generation. title: WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce
excerpt: We present WeMM-Ecom, a family of multimodal large language models that deliver frontier e-commerce capabilities while achieving state-of-the-art general-purpose performance at their respective scales. title: Composable Soft-Prompt Distillation of RL Experts: Toward Continual Post-Training
excerpt: RL post-training typically produces domain experts that must then be consolidated into one model, and as new experts keep arriving, this consolidation becomes a continual process.
